title: How does a manual test get run evidence at a commit?
description: A manual test record has no runner output, so no proof run can carry its outcome. Options: a person attests their run through the provider with the commit as subject, and the release gate requires one per manual test; the release gate ignores manual tests and the proved share counts them as lathe does; or STEGO allows no manual test in its own spec.

title: Is the committed record the published form of Service build applied, from which the fleet is read?
description: The fleet is fed by Generating's published event Service build applied, but ST-DIS-UC02-R01 says the sweep answers from the committed records alone, with no network and no service to operate. An event relay would be a service to operate. If the committed .stego/state.yaml is the event's durable form, the sweep is its projection, and the record's format version is the event's contract. Nothing raises or relays the event today.

title: Where does the registry declare the compiler range it supports, and which domain checks it?
description: ST-DIS-UC04-R04 lets the compiler pin and the registry pin move apart within a range the registry declares. The registry is Supplying's, and apply is Generating's, so Distributing can state the rule but not check it. Nothing declares or checks such a range today.

title: How does the Argo CD delivery object get its destination for each environment?
description: ST-DLV-INV10 keeps the destination cluster, namespace and overlay out of service.yaml. Options: STEGO writes one Application template and the platform's overlay patches its destination; or STEGO writes an ApplicationSet whose generator lists the platform's environment files; or the platform writes the Application and STEGO writes none.

title: What proof lets a second controller take over a provider?
description: Today one controller process owns a provider, and the model says a late result is never a success and ownership is checked again before a grant or a deletion. Automatic takeover by another process is undecided. The candidate rule: takeover starts only when the provider adapter proves that it rejects a write from the previous controller at its commit boundary, and fails closed without that proof; a replica count, a lease expiry or an operator action alone is not that proof. STEGO would own the authority contract, bounded execution, recovery state and capability checks; the adapter would supply the write precondition and its evidence; no consumer-specific lease would be required. Open: whether Keycloak and Postgres can give that proof, and whether takeover is wanted at all before replicas are.
